exposure: atypical presentations of preeclampsia and eclampsia (edema, epigastric pain, headache, visual disturbance)
family history of preeclampsia or eclampsia
cohort: The study included 57 pregnant women with atypical presentations of preeclampsia and eclampsia at Al Saudi Hospital in Khartoum, Sudan.
finding: The study demonstrated positive maternal and fetal outcomes in the management of atypical preeclampsia and eclampsia cases, with a high rate of live births and low prevalence of preterm birth and birth asphyxia.
mod_finding: Cesarean section was the most common mode of delivery (80.7%) among the participants.
